topicDisplay: Unit 3 The Study Of Shakespeare Controlled Assessment
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Whose ghost appears to Macbeth at the banquet, terrifying him in front of his guests?
questions.explain: Banquo, murdered on Macbeth's orders, returns as a ghost only Macbeth can see at the feast.

questions.q: How does the patriarchal context shape Juliet's situation with Paris?
options: Juliet is free to refuse any suitor
Lord Capulet expects to choose Juliet's husband and grows furious when she resists
questions.explain: As a daughter she is expected to obey her father, and Capulet rages when she defies the match with Paris.

questions.q: How does the Prologue describe Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explain: The Chorus calls them "a pair of star-crossed lovers", introducing the theme of fate.

questions.q: What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to do to her so she can help commit murder?
options: To protect her husband in battle
To give her the gift of prophecy
To "unsex" her and fill her with cruelty
questions.explain: She cries "unsex me here", asking to be stripped of feminine compassion to carry out the killing.

questions.q: What does the murder of a king represent in the play's idea of kingship and the divine right of kings?
options: A crime against the natural and divine order
questions.explain: Killing Duncan, God's anointed king, violates the divine order, reflected in the unnatural disturbances that follow.

questions.q: How old is Juliet in the play, reflecting Elizabethan attitudes to marriage?
questions.explain: Juliet is not yet fourteen, and her father pushes an early marriage, reflecting period customs around young brides.

questions.q: The witches warn Macbeth to beware which character?
questions.explain: The first apparition warns Macbeth to "beware Macduff".

questions.q: What is the Nurse's role in Juliet's life?
options: She is Lady Capulet's servant only
She is a spy for the Montagues
She is Juliet's confidante and former wet-nurse
questions.explain: The Nurse raised Juliet and acts as her trusted confidante and go-between with Romeo.

questions.q: How does Juliet die at the end of the play?
options: She stabs herself with Romeo's dagger
She drinks the Friar's potion again
questions.explain: Waking to find Romeo dead, Juliet stabs herself with his dagger.

questions.q: What good comes from the lovers' deaths at the play's close?
options: The Prince seizes both family estates
Verona is freed from the plague
questions.explain: The grieving families finally end their feud, reconciled by the tragedy they caused.

questions.q: In Jacobean England, the reigning monarch when Macbeth was written claimed descent from which character in the play?
questions.explain: James I traced his lineage to Banquo, which is why the witches show Banquo's descendants as future kings.

questions.q: What plan does Friar Lawrence give Juliet to avoid marrying Paris?
options: To confess the secret marriage publicly
To drink a potion that makes her appear dead
To run away to Mantua alone
questions.explain: He gives her a sleeping potion to feign death so she can later escape with Romeo.
